clue.text: Only some MPs welcome call for help to provide work for the young

indicators.note: the two outer words take in the distress signal between them, as a host welcomes a guest

parts.note: only means just, as in 'just one'
Tories are Conservative MPs, some of the members of Parliament
SOS is the Morse distress call

explanation.surface: A few parliamentarians are pleased to receive a plea for assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcome' has the outer pair hold the distress call between them. Kipling's Just So Stories is a classic children's book.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling's Just So Stories is a book written for children, so a literary work aimed at youngsters.

clue.text: Plant with flowers just opening like the one I own?

indicators.note: the opening of the word just is its first letter

parts.note: like means as, in 'as I do'
something I own is mine

explanation.surface: A gardener asks whether a blooming plant just coming into flower resembles their own.
explanation.definitionFit: Jasmine is a climbing shrub grown for its fragrant white or yellow blossoms.

clue.text: Quick to respond, as event is repeatedly moving

indicators.note: moving says these letters are shifted about into a new order
repeatedly says the little word is is taken twice over

explanation.surface: Someone is touched because an occasion is emotionally stirring again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges EVENT plus ISIS (IS given twice by 'repeatedly'); 'as' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sensitive instrument or person reacts readily to the smallest stimulus.

clue.text: Plump for an illegal occupation

definitions.meaning: plump here means short and thickset, dumpy
living in a building without the owner's permission

explanation.surface: Someone opts for a life of crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plump for' reads as 'choose', but 'Plump' is one definition and 'for' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Squat describes a short, stocky build, and as a noun it is premises occupied without legal right.

clue.text: Left home after being smothered by one of the family

indicators.note: being smothered means being wrapped round, so the word for home goes inside the relative

parts.note: a sister is a family member
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone left the house after a sibling had stifled them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after being' is linking; the home word sits just after the relative's opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister is Latin for the left-hand side, used in heraldry for the bearer's left.

clue.text: Team kit

definitions.meaning: a group working together, such as a band or firm
a set of clothes worn together

explanation.definitionFit: An outfit is both a group of people working together and a set of matching garments.

clue.text: Making a record also requires one with pizazz

parts.note: item is an old word for also, used when listing
one is the Roman numeral I
zing means energy or pizazz

explanation.surface: Producing a recording also demands someone with flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'requires' and 'with' are link words. ITEM as 'also' is an archaic usage from inventories.
explanation.definitionFit: Itemizing is listing things one by one, which is setting down a record.

clue.text: Make use of some rancorous language

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone resorts to a bit of bitter speech.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters lie in rancorouS LANGuage; 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To slang someone is to make use of abusive talk against them, an old verb sense.

clue.text: Meet in Kent area and get married in cathedral city

parts.note: Kent is a county in South East England, abbreviated SE

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation for married goes inside the city's name

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: A couple meet in south-east England and wed in a cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meet' looks like a verb but is the old adjective meaning fitting. 'get' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Meet as an adjective means proper or fitting, the same sense as decorous.

clue.text: About to smear name in tabloid? Painful effect of overexposure

indicators.note: in says these letters go inside the newspaper's name

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

indicators.note: about says the word for smearing is turned round

parts.note: to rub is to smear on

explanation.surface: A tabloid smears someone's name, and overexposure hurts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' turns the smearing word round, and 'in' puts name plus that inside the tabloid, before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Too long in strong sunlight leaves red, burnt skin.

clue.text: Middle section of Jean Genet novel describing youth

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new order
the middle section of the word Jean is its two central letters

explanation.surface: Part of a Jean Genet novel deals with youthful years.
explanation.walkthrough: EA from the middle of Jean joins GENET, and 'novel' rearranges the seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective applies to the years thirteen to nineteen, adolescence.

clue.text: Final change, in a manner of speaking, is silly

indicators.note: the final letter of the phrase's word is changed for another

parts.note: an idiom is a particular manner of speaking

explanation.surface: A last-minute alteration to some phrasing is daft.
explanation.walkthrough: IDIOM's last letter M becomes T; 'is' links. 'silly' is a noun here, as in 'you silly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A silly, as a noun, is a foolish person, a fool or dimwit.

clue.text: Actor's application will face rejection

parts.note: will in the sense of determination is spirit

indicators.note: rejection means throwing back, so the word for face is turned round

parts.note: mug is slang for face

explanation.surface: A thespian's job form is going to be turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'application' suggests a job form; it is something applied to skin. 'rejection' turns MUG into GUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirit gum is an adhesive actors use to attach false beards and moustaches.

clue.text: Reviled outlaw leader, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters might be arranged otherwise
the leader of the word outlaw is its first letter

explanation.surface: A hated bandit chief, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: REVILED plus O, the leader of outlaw, rearranged by 'perhaps'; the whole clue also describes a wrongdoer.
explanation.definitionFit: A despised bandit chief is an example of a wrongdoer.

clue.text: Breaking down after getting a bellyful

definitions.text: Breaking down after getting a bellyful

parts.words: Breaking down after getting a bellyful
parts.note: reads like a collapse after being fed up, but is the body's processing of a meal

explanation.definitionFit: The stomach breaks food down once it has been eaten.

clue.text: Important woman banned union

parts.note: big means important
Amy is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A powerful woman enters a forbidden partnership.
explanation.definitionFit: Marrying a second spouse while still wed is illegal, so a prohibited marriage.

clue.text: I riot, for a change, for a more compelling cause

indicators.note: change says these letters are altered into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A protester rampages for variety's sake, with even stronger reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' reads as one phrase, but 'for a' is fodder and 'change' the signal. The answer is Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means with still stronger reason, used of a conclusion following even more strongly.

clue.text: "Gosh", platoon leader said — or one of his men?

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation like gosh

indicators.note: the leader of the word platoon is its first letter

parts.note: oral means spoken, said

explanation.surface: A platoon commander exclaims, or perhaps a soldier under him does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is a link word; 'his' points back to the platoon leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A low-ranking NCO serves under a platoon's officer.

clue.text: Out of bed and ready to go abroad, say

definitions.text: Out of bed and ready to go

indicators.note: say signals that the word is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: abroad means away from home

explanation.surface: Up and ready for a trip overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' is the sea bed: an anchor is aweigh when just lifted from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchor raised clear of the sea floor lets a ship leave.

clue.text: Nurse drops heroin in secluded spot

indicators.note: drops means loses, so the drug's letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: to harbour a grudge is to nurse it
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A nurse gives up drugs in some quiet place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nurse' looks like a person; it is the verb, to harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A bower is a shady, sheltered garden retreat.

clue.text: Plant or animal associated with grand passion

parts.note: a fox is an animal
G is slang for a grand, a thousand
love is passion

explanation.surface: A bloom or creature linked with great ardour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' and 'associated with' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Digitalis is a tall flowering garden plant with bell-shaped blooms.

clue.text: Back last runner, not first

parts.note: the end is the last part

indicators.note: not first says the word drops its opening letter

parts.note: a horse is a runner in a race

explanation.surface: A punter backs the final horse but not the favourite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reads as betting, which fits; here it means support.
explanation.definitionFit: To support a candidate or cheque is to give it your backing.

clue.text: One who'll settle, seizing right chance

indicators.note: seizing means holding, so the abbreviation for right goes inside

parts.note: a payer settles the bill

explanation.surface: A debtor takes the right opportunity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a prayer' means no chance at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A prayer means a hope or slim possibility, as in 'not a prayer'.

clue.text: A load of software

parts.note: reads like a heap of programs, but means starting a computer by loading its programs

explanation.definitionFit: Booting a computer loads its operating system from a small start-up program.

clue.text: Old place for circus seal

parts.note: a circus is staged in a ring

explanation.surface: A performing seal at an ancient circus arena.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seal' suggests the circus animal; it is a gasket.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber loop fitted in a groove forms a watertight joint.

clue.text: Officer and Duke cut off king's escape

parts.note: a mate is a ship's officer

explanation.surface: An officer and a duke block the monarch's getaway.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess, checkmate leaves the king no escape.
explanation.definitionFit: Checkmating ends the game by leaving the king no safe square.

clue.text: Painter getting up well before noon

indicators.note: getting up in a down clue means the letters read upwards

parts.note: ten a.m. is well before noon

explanation.surface: An artist rises early in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting up' reads as rising; in a down entry it reverses TEN AM.
explanation.definitionFit: Édouard Manet was a French Impressionist artist.

clue.text: Severely practical female forsakes vanity

indicators.note: forsakes means abandons, so the female letter is dropped

parts.note: futility is vanity, pointlessness

explanation.surface: A woman gives up her vanity for plain sensible things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vanity' reads as conceit; it is the older sense of emptiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Utility clothing or furniture is plain and functional.

clue.text: Hostility only voiced in private, say

indicators.note: only voiced means only spoken, so the word is judged by sound

parts.note: a private is an example of a ranker, a soldier in the ranks

explanation.surface: Animosity expressed solely behind closed doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in private' looks like 'secretly'; 'private' is a soldier, and 'say' marks an example. 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitter, long-held resentment is enmity.

clue.text: Leader of military attack getting all-out effort?

parts.note: a general leads troops
strike means attack

explanation.surface: A commander's assault demands maximum effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all-out' is a pun: everyone comes out on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A nationwide stoppage brings all workers out together.
